answer: Sybil resistance in an agent economy rests on stake-weighted identity: every agent identity must lock a bond that scales with the influence it requests, so running ten thousand fake clones costs ten thousand real bonds. The bond is slashed when peers catch a clone voting against its own history, so an attacker's cost enters a spiral while honest payout stays flat. Newcomers start on a narrow jetty of low-value actions, earning wider permissions as independent attesters sign their record. One real plume of verified reputation outweighs a swarm of cheap aliases.
